title: Right Answer, Wrong Reason: Accuracy, Consistency, and Consensus Are Misleading Indicators of LLM Faithfulness in Clinical Decision Support
abstract: arXiv:2609.32817v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Clinical Large Language Models (LLMs) achieve strong medical-exam accuracy; however, a correct answer does not guarantee that the explanation names the concepts that actually drove the decision. We introduce three lightweight, directly interpretable metrics for this faithfulness gap: the Explanation Stability Index (ESI), which measures reasoning consistency across repeated queries; the Causal Faithfulness Score (CFS), which tests whether cited concepts drive predictions via concept ablation; and the Perturbation Stability Score (PSS), which measures robustness to semantic-preserving paraphrases. By evaluating six LLMs on 150 MedQA-USMLE questions (900 model-question observations), we found that only 23.3% of the cited clinical concepts were causally necessary. Correct answers had lower CFS than incorrect answers (0.212 vs. 0.398), answer consistency negatively predicted CFS (Spearman r = -0.466), and model pairs could agree on answe

translated_title: 正确的答案，错误的理由：准确性、一致性与共识是临床决策支持中大语言模型忠实性的误导性指标
translated_abstract: 临床大语言模型（LLMs）在医学考试中取得了较高的准确率；然而，答案正确并不能保证其解释中提及了真正驱动决策的概念。我们针对这一“忠实性差距”引入了三个轻量级、可直接解释的指标：解释稳定性指数（ESI），用于衡量重复查询中推理的一致性；因果忠实性评分（CFS），通过概念消融检验被引用的概念是否真正驱动了预测；扰动稳定性评分（PSS），用于衡量模型对保持语义的同义改述的鲁棒性。通过在150道MedQA-USMLE题目上评估六个大语言模型（共900个模型-题目观测），我们发现仅有23.3%的被引用临床概念在因果上是必要的。正确答案的CFS反而低于错误答案（0.212 对 0.398），答案一致性对CFS呈负向预测（Spearman r = -0.466），且不同模型对之间可以在答案上达成一致……
tldr: 本研究提出三个轻量级可解释指标（ESI、CFS、PSS），揭示在临床决策支持中，大语言模型答案的准确性、一致性和模型间共识并不能可靠反映其解释的因果忠实性——答案越正确因果忠实性反而越低，因此这些常见表现指标会误导对模型真实推理质量的评估。
en_tdlr: This study introduces three lightweight interpretability metrics (ESI, CFS, PSS) and shows that accuracy, consistency, and consensus are misleading indicators of LLM faithfulness in clinical decision support—correct answers exhibit lower causal faithfulness than incorrect ones, with only 23.3% of cited clinical concepts being causally necessary.
